english: O dead one, go the path; follow the Twin. The path which the Twin went, that one go. Two dogs guard the path. Do not be afraid; enter the boat. Do not turn back. May Fire receive you. May Earth cover your bones. May Dawn awaken you. May your fame be imperishable.
uncertain: néḱew: vocative of 'dead', taken as address to the dead person
yemHóm/yemHós: 'twin', taken as the name Yemo (the Twin)
mē bʰéyh₂s / mē kʷélh₁s: mē + aorist injunctive read as prohibitive 'do not'
h₁áyih₁to: middle optative of 'give' = 'receive, take'
misfit: ḱwṓ: nominative SINGULAR 'dog' after dual numeral dwóh₁; the verb h₂lékseti is also 3sg. 'Two dogs' needs a dual noun and a dual verb

english: Where is Sky? It is above. Where is Earth? It is below. What is between? Mist is between, and the sun goes between. Who was lifting him up? The great son was lifting him up. Whose son was he? He was the son of Sky and Earth.
uncertain: h₃mígʰleh₂: analyzer gives VOC.SG; taken as nominative subject (eh₂-stem nom = lemma)
h₁ím: masc. acc. 'him', taken as Sky (dyḗws)
tl̥néh₂t: imperfect 'was lifting'
h₁ést: read as past of 'be', not aorist of h₁es- 'throw'

english: The Twin spoke to the Man: 'Brother, seize me and cut me. May my flesh become the earth. May my bones become stones. May my blood become the sea. May my head become the sky. May my name be famous.' The Man heard the Twin's word and wept. His heart was trembling. Then he took a stone. Then he cut him with it. Earth and Sky came forth from him. Then the gods [gave/put] a famous name on the Twin. He departed and kept looking at the stars.
uncertain: h₂n̥réy / h₂nḗr: 'man', taken as the First Man (Manu)
bʰuh₂yéh₁t vs bʰúHyeh₁t: two different 'become' optatives (bʰweh₂- 'grow, arise' / bʰuH- 'become') used alternately; same sense
h₁íh₁: instrumental 'with it' = the stone
léytt: 'went away' or 'touched'; subject unstated (Yemo departing to the sky? or the Man?)
spéḱyet: imperfect 'kept looking at'; subject unclear
misfit: dʰh₁tóm: only 2du aorist/imperative or the participle 'placed' (nom/acc sg); with plural subject deywṓs there is no finite verb. Expected 3pl aorist (dʰh₁ént 'they placed')

english: Whose flesh is the earth? The earth is the Twin's flesh. Whose bones are the stones? The stones are his bones. Whose blood is the sea? The sea is his blood. Whose head is the sky? The sky is his head. Whose mind is the moon? The moon is his mind. Who killed the Twin? The Man killed the Twin. What was the first sacrifice? The Twin was the first sacrifice. What remains of the Twin? Imperishable fame remains from him.
uncertain: gʷʰént: imperfect 'was striking/killing' used for a completed killing; aorist would be expected for the event
némos: 'sacrifice, worship' sense chosen over 'bowing' or 'sacred place'
h₁ést: past of 'be'
misfit: yemHóns: accusative PLURAL 'twins'; 'what is left of Yemo' needs genitive yemHósyo or ablative yemHṓd (cf. answer h₁ésmōd 'from him')

english: The sons were crying out: 'Sky Father, go up! Earth Mother, lie down below! We have not seen the sun. We tremble. We are afraid.' He heard and went up. Then she lay down. The mist went away. Then it grew light. They saw the light and rejoiced. They spoke again: 'Father, giver of good things, stand above! Mother, carry us!'
uncertain: dedr̥ḱmé: perfect 1pl 'we have (not) seen' = 'we cannot see'
h₁éy: masc. nom. 'he' (Sky), not imperative 'go'
léwkt: impersonal 'it became bright'
h₁uséwōm: gen. pl. 'of good things'

english: The man saw Death. He said: 'Death, where are you going?' Death spoke: 'I have come for you. I seized your father. Now I am seizing you.' The man said: 'Do not seize me. Give me imperishable fame. I am not afraid.' Death said: 'I take; I do not give.' The man did not speak. Then he went the path.
uncertain: gʷegʷómh₂e toy: perfect 'I have come' + dat. 'to/for you'
mē me h₁éps: mē + aorist injunctive = prohibitive
kapyóh₂: 'I grasp' used absolutely ('I take')

english: The serpent was lying on the height. It seized cattle and was devouring sheep. The men were trembling. They did not eat. Then a hero arrived at the height with swift horses. Then he struck down the serpent. He freed them and drove them down from the height. They rejoiced. Then they ate. The serpent's bones lay in the field. They said: 'Hero, you slew the serpent. Your name is famous.'
uncertain: bʰérǵʰi / bʰérǵʰm̥ / bʰr̥ǵʰés: 'something high and fortified' = height/hill-fort; bʰérǵʰm̥ also parses as aor. 1sg 'I rose', rejected
gʷʰént / gʷʰéns: imperfect forms used for the completed slaying
h₁íns: masc. acc. pl. 'them' = the cattle and sheep
h₂éǵet: imperfect 'was driving'

english: The Twin lay on the bed. The gods arrived and sat around him. Then they split him open. They cut the flesh from the bones. They made the earth from it, and were breaking the bones. Then they made stones out of them. Blood ran out. Then they made waters from it. They cut off his head. Then they were fashioning the sky from it. The moon came forth from his mind. Then the clouds came forth from his tears. Then it rained. They set the sun above and threw the stars into the night. Then they saw their own work, and it was good. They were walking on her [the earth]. They drank the waters and rejoiced.
uncertain: wr̥ǵént: three homonyms (enclose / work, make / shear); 'make' chosen
h₁ésmōd: abl. 'from it' = the flesh, then the blood, then the head
kʷsépm̥: acc. 'night', read as goal 'into the night'
h₁ésyeh₂i: fem. loc. 'on her', taken as the earth
h₂wérst: impersonal 'it rained'

english: The First Man and the Twin were two brothers. Together they were driving the sheep and cattle to the pasture, and they found a bed of strewn grass under an oak. The oak was old. Then the Man was building a hearth there. He was offering poured honey to the fire. The gods spoke to him: 'Make a sacrifice! Seize your dear twin!' He heard their word, and his heart was trembling. Then he seized the Twin and struck him down. The Twin did not cry out. That was the first sacrifice. He sat down at the hearth and did not speak. Then the earth came forth from the Twin's flesh. The sky was made from his head. She [the earth] was broad. Then the sea arose from his blood. And they gave the Man good fame. He became the begetter of the people. Then the Twin's name became famous.
uncertain: h₁stā́m: 3du past of 'be' (not aorist of 'throw')
ḱóm: adverb 'together' (not deictic acc.)
stérh₃mn̥: 'strewn place, bed'
h₁ésmey: dat. 'to him'
h₁íh₂: fem. 'she', referred to the earth (dʰéǵʰōm)
dh₃ént: 3pl 'they gave'; subject unstated (the gods)

english: Sky gives water to the earth. She drinks it. Then she nourishes the herd and the sheep. The shepherd drives it [the herd] to the pasture. He milks the sheep. Wool grows from them. The men clothe themselves in wool. The dog protects them. The dog is dear to the shepherd. The wolf does not come. Then the wild beasts fled from the dog. 'Father, Mother, give us good things. Give us water and wool. Let them be many.'
uncertain: h₁íd píph₃eti: subject unstated, taken as the earth
h₁íd (2nd): neut. 'it' = the herd (h₂éǵmn̥)
h₂éǵeti: also parses as subjunctive of h₂eǵ- 'say'; 'drive' chosen
bʰugént: aorist past amid present-tense narration; 'flee' sense chosen over 'benefit'
dh₃tóm / h₁opéyetom: 2du imperatives addressing Father and Mother together
polh₁éwes h₁séntu: subject unstated (the herds?)

english: The king approached the god Werunos; then he worshipped the god.
uncertain: úpo ... sesole: tmesis 'went up to, approached'; sesóle is the perfect of *sel- (no gloss in lexicon)
wérunom: not in lexicon; read as a divine name (Werunos/Varuna) in apposition to deywóm
nú: accented form not analyzed; read as 'now/then'
h₁yaǵeto: middle past of h₁yaǵ- 'worship' (no gloss in lexicon)
no subject pronoun; the clause seems to be a fragment of a longer fable

english: The gods were hiding fire from mortals. In winter they grew cold and could not cook meat. Then a thief arrived. Then, stealing the fire at the gods' hearth, he was carrying it to the people. Night was hiding him. Then he ran to them. The thief was swift. It burned in their hearths and they grew warm. They rejoiced. They were cooking and they ate. The thief's name is [famous].
uncertain: h₁ludʰéyey: dat. sg. 'to the people' (collective)
h₁íns: masc. acc. pl. 'to them' = the mortals
studént: subject unstated, taken as the mortals
misfit: ḱlutéh₂bʰos: fem. dat./abl. PLURAL of 'famous'; nothing in the sentence is feminine plural. Expected ḱlutóm (neut. nom. sg., agreeing with h₁nómn̥) or 'famous among mortals' with a dat. pl. noun

english: Earth Mother, hear us! You who carry mortals, you who nourish the herd, you who drink the water of Sky: you are the flesh of the slain Twin. You bear the oak and the blossoms. Your fields are broad. Your wild beasts and cattle drink the waters. Give us wool and honey. Mother, may you carry us and the beasts. When we die, cover our bones.
uncertain: h₁yéh₂: fem. relative 'who' with 2sg verbs
h₁yód méromes: 'when' + subjunctive 1pl 'when we die'

english: The cattle came forth from below. Then the First Man took them. He drove them to the pasture and milked them. In winter they stood by the oak. They became many and grew. The wild beasts fled. Then the wolf arrived. Then the wolf was creeping toward them. The trusty dog caught sight of the wolf. Then the dog drove the wolf away. The man tamed the dog. The dog was dear to him. Then he yoked the team to the yoke. Now the dog sits at the hearth. The shepherd guards them.
uncertain: stn̥h₂ént: 'to place, to stand'; read intransitively 'they stood'; subject unstated (cattle?)
bʰugént: 'flee' vs 'benefit'; 'flee' chosen; why beasts flee here is unclear
h₁íns sérpet: acc. pl. 'them' as goal of creeping
ḱéywos: 'dear, intimate' (also parses as 1du of 'lie', rejected)
yugṓy yéwgos yéwgt: dat. 'to the yoke' + 'team'; subject the man

english: When night comes, the mortal lies down. Sleep seizes him. Then he awakes: Dawn awakens him. No one awakens the dead. The dead did not awaken. The dead lie in the earth. The sun shone; they have not seen it. Sleep is the brother of death.
uncertain: bʰéwdʰt: aorist 'he woke up' straight after 'sleep seizes him' and amid present-tense verbs; read as anticipating the dawn
kʷis ne: indefinite + ne = 'no one'
h₁íd: neut. 'it' = the sun (sóh₂wl̥ is neuter)
supnós: 'sleep' (lexicon also 'death')

english: The sheep said to the horses: 'My heart pains me, seeing a man driving horses.'
uncertain: whole item: older unaccented, laryngeal-free notation (Schleicher-style), unlike the rest of the packet; the analyzer recognizes only eweukʷet, ḱerd, moi
eweukʷet: augmented aorist 'said'
agʰnutai: not in lexicon; read as middle 'is pained, grieves'
widn̥tei: dat. participle 'to (me) seeing'
ǵʰm̥onm̥: acc. 'man (earthling)'
aǵontm̥: acc. participle 'driving'

english: The old man died. His wife and his sister wept and laid him on the bed. Then they were carrying him to the fire. The old man's flesh was burning. Then the earth received his bones. They said: 'Father, we remember you. May your name be famous.' Then they were offering poured honey to him. They sat down at the hearth.
uncertain: péh₂wr̥: bare neut. 'fire' read as goal 'to the fire'
h₁éwset: 'burn', read intransitively 'was burning'
memn̥mé: perfect 1pl 'we remember'
h₁áyto: middle aorist 'received'

english: Fire was hidden in the stone. No one knew it. [A man?] sat down on it and struck it with a stone. Then it [the fire] ran out. He trembled. Then he rejoiced. He put meat into water. It was boiling and shining. Then the men arrived at it. They sat around it. They ate and were sated.
uncertain: h₁ésmi: loc. 'on it' (not 1sg 'I am')
h₁ím ... h₂ḱmnéh₁: 'it' (the stone, masc.) struck 'with a stone'
Hwért: 'enclose, put, insert' = put meat into water
léwkt: 'became bright', subject unclear (water? fire?)
misfit: l̥h₂tós: masc. nom. sg. 'hidden' with the neuter subject péh₂wr̥; expected neuter l̥h₂tóm
wiHróns: acc. PLURAL 'men' as the subject of 3sg intransitive sédt 'sat down' (and of the following stunédt); expected nom. sg. wiHrós

english: Then the Man was leading the Twin to the bed. The Twin was looking at the bed. He spoke: 'I see fire and the oak. Where are the sheep? Where are the cattle?' The Man said: 'Brother, you are the sacrifice.' Then the Twin became afraid. He did not flee, and lay down on the bed. Then the Man killed him. His heart was trembling. His blood ran out over the bed. Then the earth drank it. Then it was growing dark. The stars shone. Then the Man stood up there. He did not see his brother.
uncertain: wédʰet: 'lead' vs homonym 'bind, marry'; 'lead' chosen
stérh₃mn̥ (with h₁éǵʰs dʰénh₂t): acc. 'bed', read as 'over/onto the bed'
h₁ésyo ḱḗr trémt: 'his', ambiguous between the Man and the Twin
h₁regʷesyét: impersonal 'it was growing dark'

english: The Twin lay down and did not stand up. Then he died. He was the first mortal. No one knew the path. He found it and went along it. The path was long. He did not turn back. Then they followed him. Now the Twin leads the dead along the path. He is king of the dead. His name is famous. His fame is imperishable.
uncertain: h₁ím: masc. acc. = the path (stóygʰos)
sékʷonto: 3pl 'they followed', subject unstated (the dead / later mortals)
stóygʰom: acc. 'path', read as 'along the path'

english: Night, come to the people and the herd! You who cover the earth, who carry the stars. Your stars look at the people. The moon climbs above. Cover mortals and beasts! Sleep has come to us and to the beasts. You are mother of the stars and of Dawn. Night, do not frighten us or our herd. May Dawn, daughter of Sky, come to us.
uncertain: ḱélesi: 2sg present 'you cover' (or subjunctive of ḱel- 'conceal')
gʷémt: aorist 'came'
nos h₂éǵmn̥: nos read as gen. 'our herd' (or acc. 'us, the herd')
mē troséyes: mē + past/injunctive 2sg = prohibitive

english: Sky and Earth were lying together. The sons were dwelling between them. They were trembling. Then they grew strong. Then the great son stood up. He looked at them and spoke: 'Let us lift up the Sky. Let us set her [Earth] down.' Standing, they lifted him up and set her down. Then it grew light. Then the mist went away. They saw the sun and rejoiced. He was standing above; she was lying below. The sun goes between.
uncertain: ḱóm: adverb 'together'
tḱiyént: 'dwell, settle'
tl̥néh₂omes / sodéyōmes: subjunctive 1pl 'let us'
h₁ím / h₁íh₂m̥: masc. = Sky, fem. = Earth

english: Night comes and day comes. The sun climbs in the day. The stars stand in the sky. Winter comes, and the waters grew cold. The days grow long. Heat dries the waters. The sun turned and winter went away. The snows melt and blossoms arose in the field. The sheep grew and the horses grew. Who arranged this for the people and the beasts? The gods arranged this for them.
uncertain: studént: aorist among present-tense verbs
h₂ékʷeh₂es: nom. pl. (also gen. sg.)
Héh₂mr̥h₂ dl̥h₁gʰéh₂: neut. pl. subject with 3sg verb, regular
bʰwéh₂t: 3sg with neut. pl. h₂éndʰōs, regular
h₁éḱwōs: nom. pl. 'horses'
misfit: snóygʷʰōs: masc. nom. PLURAL 'snows' with 3sg verb tinéh₁ti; expected snóygʷʰos (sg.) or 3pl tinh₁énti

english: The wheel of the sun goes in the sky. Swift horses pull the wheel. The sun's wheel is swift. Dawn grew bright, then the sun shone. The sun sank in the night and shone in the day. The sun's wheel does not break. Its path is straight. The sun warms the waters. The sun sees us and the beasts. May the sun see us; may it hear us.
uncertain: Hrumptór: middle present 'is (not) broken / does not break'
h₁ésyo: 'its' = the wheel's or the sun's
dedórḱe: perfect 'has seen' = 'sees'
h₁íd: neut. 'it' = the sun

english: May the cattle stand there; may they not flee. May the wolf not come to them. May the snake and the thief not seize them. Dog, protect the sheep and the herd! Shepherd, drive them inside! Sky, give water! Earth, nourish them! May they become many, may they grow. May the king have imperishable fame. May the king's herd be great and large.
uncertain: h₁pyéh₁t: 3sg optative with two subjects (snake and thief); singular agreement with the nearer subject is possible
h₃rēǵéy: dat. 'to the king' = 'may the king have'
méǵh₂ polh₁ú: neuter, agreeing with h₂éǵmn̥

english: Dawn, daughter of Sky, shine forth! You who awaken the people and the beasts, who drive away the night, who bring the swift light of the sun. You wear a broad garment. When you come, the night grows less. Your light is great. Dawn, come to our hearth. Dawn, daughter of Sky, awaken us.
uncertain: h₂usdʰí: 2sg imperative 'shine (at dawn)'
pl̥th₂uyéh₂h₁ pĺ̥h₂seh₂h₁: instrumental 'with a broad garment' with middle 'wear'
minéwti: 'lessen' used intransitively 'grows less'
nos h₂éHsh₂m̥: nos read as gen. 'our hearth'
h₂éǵesi: also parses as subjunctive of 'say'; 'drive' chosen

english: Desire arose first; mind arose from desire. Who was stretching out the sky? Who was laying the earth below? Who made the sea and the oak? Who set the sun and the moon above? Who yoked swift horses to the sun's wheel? Who gave mortals day and light? The gods know it, and we do not know it. Let us make sacrifice to them.
uncertain: pr̥h₂wós: nom. adj. 'first', used adverbially
wérǵt: 'make' chosen among the homonyms
wérǵomes: subjunctive 1pl 'let us make' or present 1pl 'we make'
widḗr / widmé: perfect 'know'

english: A sheep that had no wool saw horses: one pulling a heavy wagon, one carrying a great load, one carrying a man quickly.
uncertain: whole item: older unaccented, laryngeal-free notation (Schleicher-style); the analyzer recognizes only ne, dedorḱe, bʰorom, bʰerontn̥s
yesmin wl̥nā ne ēst: relative 'on whom wool was not' = 'that had no wool'
wegʰontn̥s / bʰerontn̥s: acc. pl. participles agreeing with eḱwons; 'one... one...' distributive reading
meǵHm, gʷr̥um, monum, ōḱu: 'great', 'heavy', 'man', 'quickly' (not in analyzer)
